---
title: "Using spatialDWLS from Giotto"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
show <- function(name) {
  cat(readLines(file.path("figures", name)), sep = "\n")
}
```

[Giotto](https://giottosuite.com) calls spatialDWLS through
`runDWLSDeconv()`, so a Giotto user never touches the matrices directly: the
expression, clusters and result all stay in the Giotto object. This article
shows that workflow on the small Visium dataset that ships with GiottoData.
For the same method on plain matrices, see
[Get started](https://drieslab.github.io/spatialDWLS/articles/spatialDWLS.html).

> The outputs on this page were computed locally and saved, because building
> them needs Giotto, GiottoData and a Giotto environment. The script that
> produced them is
> [`dev/render-giotto-article.R`](https://github.com/drieslab/spatialDWLS/blob/main/dev/render-giotto-article.R).

## Setup

spatialDWLS is a suggested package of Giotto, so install both:

```{r install}
remotes::install_github("drieslab/spatialDWLS")
# and Giotto: https://giottosuite.com/articles/installation.html
```

```{r load}
library(Giotto)

g <- GiottoData::loadGiottoMini("visium")
```

The mini object is a small mouse brain Visium section that has already been
normalised and clustered (`leiden_clus`).

## 1. A signature matrix

spatialDWLS needs the mean expression of each cell type over a set of
signature genes. In a real analysis that comes from a **single-cell
reference** of the same tissue, for example with
`makeSignMatrixDWLSfromMatrix()` on the reference's normalised expression and
its cell type labels.

GiottoData has no matching single-cell reference, so for this demonstration
the "cell types" are the Visium clusters themselves and the signature genes
are their top markers. That is enough to show the workflow; it is not how to
get biologically meaningful cell types.

```{r signature}
markers <- findMarkers_one_vs_all(g, method = "scran",
                                  cluster_column = "leiden_clus",
                                  min_feats = 20)
sign_gene <- unique(markers[, head(feats, 20), by = "cluster"]$V1)

meta <- pDataDT(g)
sign_matrix <- makeSignMatrixDWLS(g,
  sign_gene = sign_gene,
  cell_type_vector = paste0("type_", meta$leiden_clus)
)
dim(sign_matrix)
```
```{r, echo = FALSE, eval = TRUE, comment = "#>"}
show("sign-matrix-dim.txt")
```

## 2. Deconvolve

```{r deconvolve}
g <- runDWLSDeconv(g,
  sign_matrix = sign_matrix,
  cluster_column = "leiden_clus",
  n_cell = 10
)
```

The proportions are stored in the object as a spatial enrichment named
`"DWLS"`, one row per spot:

```{r result}
getSpatialEnrichment(g, name = "DWLS", output = "data.table")
```
```{r, echo = FALSE, eval = TRUE, comment = "#>"}
show("dwls-head.txt")
```

`runDWLSDeconv()` takes the same settings as `spatialDWLS::dwls()`:

- `n_cell`: expected cells per spot. A cell type is kept for a spot in the
  second round only when its first-round share is at least `1 / n_cell`.
- `cutoff`: the enrichment score a cell type must reach in a cluster to be
  considered there.
- `BPPARAM`: run the per-spot solves in parallel, e.g.
  `BPPARAM = BiocParallel::MulticoreParam(8)`. Without it, Giotto's session
  default (`GiottoUtils::giotto_bpparam()`) is used.
- `na_as_zero`: spots with no signal on the signature genes are `NA` by
  default.

## 3. Plot

`spatDeconvPlot()` draws each spot as a pie of its cell type proportions:

```{r pies}
spatDeconvPlot(g, deconv_name = "DWLS", pie_scale = 0.4)
```
```{r, echo = FALSE, eval = TRUE, out.width = "100%", fig.alt = "Spatial pie chart of cell type proportions per Visium spot."}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/giotto-deconv-pies.png")
```

The proportions are ordinary columns, so anything else is a short step away,
e.g. colouring spots by their dominant cell type:

```{r dominant}
dwls <- getSpatialEnrichment(g, name = "DWLS", output = "data.table")
type_cols <- setdiff(names(dwls), "cell_ID")
dominant <- type_cols[max.col(as.matrix(dwls[, type_cols, with = FALSE]))]

g <- addCellMetadata(g,
  new_metadata = data.frame(cell_ID = dwls$cell_ID, dominant_type = dominant),
  by_column = TRUE, column_cell_ID = "cell_ID"
)
spatPlot2D(g, cell_color = "dominant_type", point_size = 2.5)
```
```{r, echo = FALSE, eval = TRUE, out.width = "85%", fig.alt = "Visium spots coloured by their dominant cell type."}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/giotto-dominant-type.png")
```

## Disk-backed objects

A Giotto object whose expression is held on disk by
[GiottoDisk](https://github.com/giotto-suite/GiottoDisk) goes through the
same `runDWLSDeconv()` call. GiottoDisk reads the signature genes one window
of spots at a time and hands them to `spatialDWLS::dwls_stream()`, so the
result is the same while the expression never has to fit in memory.
